answer: Each identity seals a storage plot: tags are keyed to its secret, and each epoch audits offsets in a spiral through it. Layered like a lotus, the erasure coding ensures one stored copy cannot answer two identities' challenges, since audits demand tags recomputed under a different key. A ferrous seal fails loudly when a clone reuses another plot, and failed spot checks drop the seat. A farm must provision and maintain a full plot per clone; the marginal cost never discounts with fleet size, so pooled copies mint no extra seats and influence tracks genuinely provisioned storage.
